**Repaired finding submitted: Compliant (no redline).**

I extended the search to close the contingency the verifier flagged (a verification or true-up right hiding in fee/reporting provisions or schedules):

- **§ 11 Fees (p0084)** — bare payment obligation keyed to the Fee Schedule; no reporting, reconciliation or verification right.
- **§ 2 Grant of License** — conditions use outside Authorized Locations on "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule," but gives Garman no inspection or audit mechanism to test compliance.
- **Schedules A–F (§ 1, p0019–p0026)** — incorporated as an integral part of the Agreement, but summary-titled only (Fee Schedule; Software and Documentation; Authorized Locations; Specifications/Modifications/Data Conversion; Implementation and Training; Telephone Support). No reporting, usage-return or verification machinery appears in the available text.
- **§ 17(b) (p0118)** — the only certification obligation: a one-off post-termination self-certification that Software, Documentation and Codes have been destroyed or returned. That is a customary wind-down confirmation given by us, not a recurring vendor audit, and it involves no vendor entry, no third-party auditor and no system access.
- **§ 3, § 14, § 20** — as previously cited: use restrictions, confidentiality treatment of accounting records, and notices boilerplate respectively.

Result unchanged: no audit right binds us, so the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost, system access) cannot arise, and our position is at least as favorable as the playbook's preferred outcome. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check necessarily fails where no audit clause exists; adding limits would require first creating the vendor right they constrain, so the correct edit is none.
